sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Delaware County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Two offices in the same Delaware building split the work. The county auditor sets values and runs the relief programs, and the county treasurer bills and collects. Both sit at 145 N. Union St., 1st floor, Delaware, OH 43015, and both keep weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The recorder works from the same street address and files deeds, while a three-member Board of Revision hears value complaints. A seller who owes tax will deal with the treasurer for the balance and with the auditor for anything about value or credits.

Delaware County offices that touch a home sale (from the county auditor, treasurer and recorder websites)
OfficePhoneHandles
Auditor(740) 833-2900Values, homestead forms, Board of Revision filings, rates of taxation
Treasurer(740) 833-2480Tax bills, payments, escrow, penalty remission, tax lien sales

sections.h2: What is Delaware County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Delaware County is a fast-growing suburban and rural county that sits just north of Franklin County and the state capital. The Census Bureau counts 242,032 residents in its July 2025 estimate, up 13.0% from the 2020 base, and it lists 95,340 housing units. The county covers 443 square miles of land, and the Olentangy River, Alum Creek and the Scioto run through it from north to south, according to Wikipedia.

QuickFacts shows a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied value of $445,500 and a median household income of $133,540. Owners live in 78.5% of occupied homes, and the Census lists 2,016 building permits for 2025.

Towns inside the county include the city of Delaware (the seat), Powell, Sunbury, and parts of Dublin and Westerville, plus the villages of Ashley, Galena, Ostrander and Shawnee Hills. The school district shapes the tax bill. The treasurer's June 2026 notice singles out Dublin, Westerville and Olentangy as districts whose residential parcels did not receive the new inflation cap credit.

sections.h2: When are Delaware County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is paid in two halves. For the bills payable in 2027, the treasurer's website lists February 10, 2027 for the first half and July 12, 2027 for the second half. The tax is billed in arrears, so the 2025 tax year bills were the ones payable in 2026.

  • The 2025 second-half deadline was moved from July 10 to August 17, 2026, because House Bill 186 had to be applied to the bills first.
  • The treasurer's June 2026 notice says the extension applied to 2026 only and that collections go back to the February 10 and July 10 pattern.
  • Forms on the treasurer's site include the 2 1/2% reduction, escrow or ACH automatic deduction, homestead, penalty remission, property valuation complaint and a tax mailing address change.
  • A parcel's payment history is on the auditor's property record under the Tax tab, at the bottom of the Tax Detail screen.

Questions on a specific bill go to the treasurer at (740) 833-2480.

sections.h2: What did House Bill 186 change on Delaware County bills?
sections.html:
House Bill 186 created an Inflation Cap Credit that lowers taxes on certain school district levies, and the credit was applied retroactively to tax year 2025 for real property. According to the treasurer's announcement, residential and agricultural parcels receive it everywhere in the county except in the Dublin, Westerville and Olentangy school districts.

Owners who qualified and had already paid in full see any overpayment applied to the following tax year. The credit shows as its own line on the second-half bill and on the property record at the auditor's site. The treasurer also posted a summary of the bill on its home page. A seller preparing a listing should pull the parcel's tax detail from the auditor's site rather than quote an old bill to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my value with the Delaware County Board of Revision?
sections.html:
File a formal complaint with the auditor between January 2 and March 31. The auditor's Board of Revision page explains that the board reviews value as of the January 1 lien date and does not hear complaints about the tax rate or the taxes themselves. Under Ohio Revised Code 5715.19, the statutory cutoff is March 31 or the close of first-half collection, whichever is later.

The auditor's 2026 Triennial Valuation Update page says the informal review window has ended and names March 31, 2027 as the last day for a formal complaint against the value as of January 1, 2027. The auditor accepts filings in person or by mail at 145 N. Union St., by email to auditor@co.delaware.oh.us, or by fax at (740) 833-2899.

  • A recent independent appraisal, photos of damage, comparable sales, and the closing statement and purchase contract for a recent sale are the items the board lists as helpful.
  • Hearings follow court-style rules, with sworn witnesses and marked exhibits, and normally last 10 to 20 minutes.
  • Decisions are held for 30 days. A further appeal goes to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the Delaware County Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of the decision letter.
  • The board will not lower a value by comparing it with the auditor's values for neighbors where no arm's length sale took place.

sections.h2: Which Delaware County tax relief programs matter when selling?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one, and it travels with the owner rather than the house. The auditor's homestead page says it reduces taxes by the amount that would otherwise be charged on $25,000 of market value for owners who are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled, on up to one acre. New applicants face an income test. Anyone who received the credit for tax year 2013 skips the test and keeps the credit after moving to another Ohio home.

Ohio law also builds a disclosure step into the deed process. Under ORC 319.202, the buyer's value statement must confirm that the seller was asked whether the property gets a tax reduction under section 323.152(A) and whether it was in current agricultural use valuation. If it was, the paperwork has to account for the lost reduction or the recoupment charge before the auditor endorses the deed.

sections.h2: What should I do about unpaid Delaware County property tax before I sell?
sections.html:
Ask the treasurer's office for the exact balance before you set a price, and ask your closing agent to request a payoff figure so the tax is paid from the sale. The treasurer's website carries a Tax Lien Sales page with a tax lien certificate sale policy, and the auditor's site has a Forfeited Land Sales page, so a long delinquency can end in a county process.

The treasurer's forms page lists a Penalty Remission form. Call (740) 833-2480 to ask whether it applies to a given parcel. Owners who are behind and short on time can also line up a buyer first and let the closing statement show the tax balance as a line item.

faqs.q: Where is the Delaware County auditor's office?
faqs.a: It is at 145 N. Union St., 1st floor, Delaware, OH 43015, and the phone is (740) 833-2900. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Delaware County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Delaware County Treasurer at (740) 833-2480. The treasurer shares the 145 N. Union St. building with the auditor and takes questions on payments, escrow and penalties.

faqs.q: Who can file a Delaware County value complaint?
faqs.a: The owner of taxable real property in the county, the owner's spouse, and a retained professional such as a licensed appraiser, broker or public accountant can file, under ORC 5715.19. The form is on the auditor's forms page, and the Board of Revision handles value only, not the rate.

faqs.q: Did every Delaware County owner get the Inflation Cap Credit?
faqs.a: No. The treasurer's notice says residential and agricultural parcels received it except those in the Dublin, Westerville and Olentangy school districts, and not every property qualifies.

faqs.q: What is the Delaware County property tax rate?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel's school district, township or city, and voted levies. The auditor posts a Rates of Taxation page and an Effective Tax Rates page, and the parcel's own record shows its figures.
